name: Motorcycle
description: A vehicle with a saddle for the rider designed to travel on no more than three wheels, including motor scooters and motor-driven bicycles but not mopeds or electric assisted bicycles. An electric two-wheeler that can go faster than 30 mph is one.

restrictions.rule: A saddle for the rider, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Takes in motor scooters and motor-driven bicycles; excludes mopeds and electric assisted bicycles
An electric two- or three-wheeler that can go faster than 30 mph on a level surface is past the moped limit and is a motorcycle
Riders need a regular or full provisional driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle learner's permit; the permit is open from 16 with a full provisional license
Riders 18 and older earn the endorsement with a knowledge test and a road test or an approved rider course
Riders under 18 with an endorsement may not carry a passenger
Riders and passengers must wear a safety helmet meeting FMVSS 218, with the retention strap secured
Titled and registered with the DMV like a car
Carries no more people than it was designed for
North Carolina's all-terrain vehicle law covers only vehicles on three or more low-pressure tires, so an off-road e-moto has no separate off-highway category
